decisions.reason: The source changes only the need and placement of ESP32 breakout holes; it does not change I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, or wiring.
The relevant mechanical impact is already fully captured by the existing same-message MODIFY stating that unused-pin holes may be placed anywhere rather than around the ESP32.
The source refers to physical breakout holes for otherwise-unused pins and does not reassign GPIOs or change pin compatibility rules.
Flexible placement of unused-pin breakout holes does not alter the BOOT button, reset connection, or associated capacitance.
The source does not change any panel input, GPIO assignment, or connector-mounted control.
The referenced holes are ESP32 unused-pin breakout holes on the main board, not the power-board mounting holes relevant to battery connector clearance.
The breakout-hole clarification does not change the standalone regulator, powered load, source selection, or USB operating condition.
The source contains no change to DCDC1 voltage configuration or 3.3V rail regulation.
The source concerns unused ESP32 pin holes on the main board, not power-board mounting holes, dimensions, orientation, or connector access.
The clarification does not change any interboard connector type, pinout, pin order, or power-distribution topology.
The source applies to ESP32 unused-pin breakout holes on the main board and does not alter the sensor-board layout.
The source does not change the sensor-board connector inventory, module interfaces, pinouts, or connector count.
